claims.text: A controlled heat treatment can induce fine nanoscale precipitates and thereby create a dual-phase microstructure in an initially single-phase high-entropy alloy.
The induced precipitates can be coherent or semi-coherent L1₂ or B2 phases.
Specific heat-treatment temperatures and durations can control precipitate size and distribution.
Under-treatment may produce incomplete development of the dual-phase microstructure.
Over-treatment or over-aging may coarsen the precipitates and eliminate their mechanical benefits.
The heat treatment produces nanoscale coherent or semi-coherent precipitates dispersed within the matrix.
The precipitates interact with dislocations.
The precipitation treatment refines the grain structure.
The precipitates impede dislocation motion and increase yield and tensile strengths through precipitation strengthening.
The dual-phase structure promotes strain accommodation at phase interfaces.
The dual-phase structure promotes energy dissipation at phase interfaces.
Interfacial strain accommodation and energy dissipation enhance ductility.
Interfacial strain accommodation and energy dissipation enhance Young's modulus.
Interfacial strain accommodation and energy dissipation enhance fracture resistance.
Optimized heat-treated specimens will have approximately 10–20% higher yield strength than untreated single-phase specimens.
Optimized heat-treated specimens will have approximately 10–20% higher tensile strength than untreated single-phase specimens.
Optimized heat-treated specimens will have approximately 10–20% higher fracture toughness than untreated single-phase specimens.
Optimized heat-treated specimens will maintain or slightly improve ductility relative to untreated single-phase specimens.
The proposed benefits should hold at ambient and moderate service temperatures.
Extended high-temperature exposure may drive precipitate coarsening and negate the proposed benefits.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis asserts enhanced ductility, whereas the predicted outcome allows ductility merely to be maintained.

The predicted 10–20% range applies to yield strength, tensile strength, and fracture toughness, with only maintained or slightly improved ductility and no quantified modulus gain; the falsification rule ambiguously applies a consistent 10–20% enhancement to the combined set of strength, ductility, modulus, and fracture resistance.
